content.title: All the NBA Games on NBC & Peacock This Week (April 5-7): Lakers, Warriors & More
content.text: This week brings a loaded slate of NBA on NBC and Peacock games, featuring legends like the Los Angeles Lakers' LeBron James, rising stars like the Dallas Mavericks' Cooper Flagg, and plenty of teams still jockeying for post-season positioning.How to WatchThe full lineup this week tips off with the Los Angeles Lakers vs. Dallas Mavericks and Houston Rockets vs. Golden State Warriors on Sunday Night Basketball on NBC and Peacock; then on Monday there’s the New York Knicks vs. Atlanta Hawks streaming on Peacock. Finally, Coast 2 Coast Tuesday brings a loaded doubleheader featuring the Charlotte Hornets vs. Boston Celtics and the Houston Rockets vs. Phoenix Suns.RELATED: How Do the NBA Playoffs & Play-In Tournament Work in 2026? What to KnowThe slate is loaded with playoff implications, as eight of the teams featuring in NBC Sports’ five-game lineup are all still in contention and vying for playoff positioning as we head into the final week of the NBA regular season. After that? The playoffs begin.Sunday, April 5, 7:30 p.m.: Lakers at Mavericks (NBC, Peacock)Sunday, April 5, 10 p.m.: Rockets at Warriors (NBC, Peacock)Monday, April 6. 7 p.m.: Knicks at Hawks (Peacock)Tuesday, April 7, 8 p.m.: Hornets at Celtics (NBC, Peacock)Tuesday, April 7, 11 p.m.: Rockets at Suns (NBC, Peacock)The final installment of Sunday Night Basketball this season brings a stacked doubleheader, with the Lakers taking on the Mavericks from American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas. The second game of the night will feature NBA All-Star Kevin Durant and the Rockets headed to California to take on the Warriors. Steph Curry, who hasn’t played since late January, remains a game-time decision to potentially return from a knee injury. NBC Sports’ Mike Tirico (play-by-play), Jamal Crawford (analyst), and Ashley ShahAhmadi (courtside reporter) will call Lakers-Mavericks. NBC Sports’ Noah Eagle (play-by-play), Reggie Miller (analyst), and Grant Liffmann (courtside reporter) will call Rockets-Warriors.Peacock NBA Monday will find six-time NBA All-Star Karl-Anthony Towns and the Knicks taking on the Hawks from State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Georgia. The game will feature the last NBC Sports' “On the Bench” coverage of the season, with analysts embedded on each team’s bench. Jordan Cornette will be dedicated to the Hawks’ bench, and Austin Rivers will be with the Knicks.Fans watching on mobile can also use Peacock's new Live Vertical Video view available within the Courtside Live feature. The beta feature presents the full game in a vertical video format within Courtside Live, offering curated alternate game angles to give fans a behind-the-scenes look at the action. The NBA on NBC action all comes to a head on Tuesday night with Coast 2 Coast Tuesday, featuring primetime games on NBC airing live in each market (with both games streaming nationwide on Peacock). Jayson Tatum, Jaylen Brown and the Boston Celtics will start things off, hosting the Charlotte Hornets from TD Garden in Boston, Massachusetts. The final game of the night finds Kevin Durant and the Houston Rockets heading to Phoenix to take on five-time NBA All-Star Devin Booker and the Suns from Mortgage Matchup Center. NBC Sports’ Noah Eagle (play-by-play), Reggie Miller (analyst), and Ashley ShahAhmadi (courtside reporter) will call Hornets-Celtics. NBC Sports’ John Fanta (play-by-play), Derek Fisher (analyst), and Zora Stephenson (courtside reporter) will call Rockets-Suns.
